title: kinframe plugin view, API 1
description: What a plugin's render() and detail() return (docs/plugins.md §4). The frame draws it natively; anything that does not validate is not drawn and the previous view stays. Limits beyond what JSON Schema can express: the tree is at most 3 components deep (stack › stack › leaf), a view has at most 24 components in total (rows' values included, flow nodes not), edge ids must name nodes of the same flow, node ids are unique, sparkline min < max, strings have no line breaks or control characters, and the serialized view is at most 16 KB. The Kotlin validator (android/core/.../PluginViewParser.kt) enforces all of them.

none.description: Nothing to show right now (the music stopped): the widget is hidden and its place in the band freed. Only as the whole view. Returning null instead keeps the last view.

image.description: A picture (album art, a snapshot) from an http(s) URL the plugin's own network permissions allow. The frame fetches it (at most 768 KB), decodes it small and caches it; a quiet placeholder until then. Square (rounded corners) or round; the size comes from the form.

actions.description: Round icon buttons that call the plugin's action(ctx, id) handler. Tappable in the detail card only (the corner and the band don't draw them). Needs permissions.actions in the manifest.

progress.description: A thin bar from min (default 0) to max, or a marker dot on the track. While running, the frame moves the value on by one per second from `at` (epoch ms), so a track's position moves smoothly between refreshes; `time` shows seconds as 1:23 / 3:45.

tone.description: Maps to the frame's palette (lightened on photos). Default neutral; a container's tone is the default for its children. The first six say how good something is; water, gas and heat name a quantity (pair them with their icon: colour is never the only cue).

list.description: Up to 5 rows of time, title, detail and badge: departures, bin days, appointments. Corner: a label and the first 3 rows; detail card: all rows; band column (too narrow for titles): the first row's icon and the times with their badges (the first title when no row has a time); band strip: the first 2 rows, one line each. A row's tone colours its badge and icon.

icon.description: The fixed icon set of API 1, drawn by the frame in its line style. `direction` is a needle pointing up (north), meant to be turned with a value's `icon_rotation`.

value.description: Icon, big number, unit, optional label and trend arrow: ⚡ 1,2 kW ↑. Format numbers with ctx.format; a unit after a (no-break) space in `value` is drawn smaller unless `unit` is given. One or two decimals are drawn small and raised (21,4 → 21 with a raised ,4); the text itself is unchanged.

icon_rotation.description: Turns the icon clockwise by this many degrees, e.g. the `direction` needle for a wind direction (pointing where the wind blows to). Absent: upright.

rows.description: Up to 4 values stacked: grid / solar / home.

gauge.description: A ring (default) or bar from 0–100 % with a short label inside: car battery 68 %. A dial is two-sided: zero at the top, -100–100 %, positive clockwise in `tone`, negative anticlockwise in `negative_tone` (grid use vs return); a trailing unit in its label is drawn small below the number.

sub.description: Up to three small values under a ring or dial: today's ↑ 11,8 / ↓ 14,5 kWh beside the live power.

flow.description: Up to 5 nodes with animated arrows between them; arrow speed follows power (relative to the largest edge). The node with the most edges is drawn in the middle.

percent.description: A ring around the node (0–100), e.g. a home battery's charge.

power.description: A magnitude; 0 draws an idle line. Swap from/to for the other direction.

sparkline.description: A small chart of 2–100 points (a day of quarter hours, 100 on the day the clocks go back); null is a gap. `bars` draws a bar per point from zero (or the range's nearest edge). `highlight` picks out one point in `highlight_tone` (default the chart's tone), `marker` another as "now" (a thin line across the chart); both are indexes of numbers, not gaps.

text.description: One or two short lines: Charging · full at 23:10.

stack.description: A vertical (default) or horizontal group. In the band the frame picks the axis: a column stacks vertically, a strip horizontally.
